decisions.reason: The BOM state still requires R10 and R11 to be retained as 0-ohm I2C protection resistors, while the source revises them to optional 22-ohm series resistors that may be omitted when they impede layout.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
The 22Ω resistors on SDA/SCL are just for signal quality. I2C lines are open-drain — when released, the pull-up resistor has to charge the cable capacitance back to 3.3V, which can cause a small overshoot/ringing at
the transition edge. The resistor damps that.

For our cables (10–20cm), it's not really a problem — rise time will be well within spec with the 2.2kΩ pull-ups. So if they're making layout harder, you can remove them. If they're already placed and not in the
way, keep them. Either way is fine.

value_updates.approved_r10_r11_justification: R10 and R11 are 22-ohm SDA/SCL series resistors for signal-quality damping of overshoot and ringing.
value_updates.r10_r11_population_policy: Optional; retain if already placed and not obstructing layout, otherwise omit.

decisions.reason: The decision changes SDA/SCL series-resistor conditioning, not the interboard connector partition, connector types, signal pinout, or pin-order policy.
The optional I2C series resistors do not change the standalone USB regulator, source selection, powered rail, or programming behavior.
The source concerns SDA/SCL signal conditioning and does not alter the charge-status LED connector, resistor, GPIO, or population requirements.
The revised I2C series-resistor policy does not affect the battery-protection controller, cutoff voltages, or DW01A protection resistors R7 and R8.
The sensor board remains a connector fanout regardless of whether the separate SDA/SCL conditioning resistors are populated.
The source affects only SDA/SCL conditioning and does not change USB D+/D− enumeration, connector sourceability, or interboard USB routing.
The I2C resistor decision does not alter the addressable LEDs' 5V supply, GPIO, level shifting, or standby-power control.
The source confirms compatibility with the existing 3.3V pull-ups but does not change DCDC1 voltage, current rating, or powered-load role.
The optional SDA/SCL series resistors are independent of the switchable 5V boost rail, its enable GPIO, pull-down, and powered loads.
Permission to omit resistors if they impede layout does not change the established connector placement, orientation, access, or mounting-hole clearance requirements.
The SDA/SCL signal-conditioning decision does not affect the battery NTC terminal, connector, monitoring function, or controller.
